title: Moza MA3F Airbus Sidestick review: real Airbus feel on a Force Feedback Base?
description:
hen you disconnect the autopilot at 500 feet on a gusty manual approach, you have exactly one job: trust your stick inputs. But while looking like an authentic airliner cockpit replica is one thing, how does an officially licensed Airbus side stick actually handle when mounted to an active force feedback base?

Enter the Moza MA3F Airbus Sidestick Grip. Officially licensed by Airbus and modeled after the captain's side stick, this grip is built from ultra-rigid composite rated for 30 kg of static load, locks down securely with a 5-pin aviation collar, and features an ingenious swappable magnetic cover to switch between a practical 5-way camera hat and a clean, purist silhouette.

In this deep-dive hardware review and flight test, we put the Moza MA3F through its paces on the Moza AB6 force feedback base. We examine build quality and shell ergonomics, walk through the essential Moza Cockpit software setup to tune linear response curves for Airbus fly-by-wire logic, and take it into Microsoft Flight Simulator for real-world testing in the FlyByWire A320. 

Crucially, we tackle the reality of flying this stick day-to-day:
- Manual Hand-Flying & Landings: Evaluating centering precision, rate-demand control handoff, and micro-corrections on final approach.
- The Modular Hat Switch: Comparing the utility of the 9-input 5-way hat for view panning against the flush magnetic blanking cap.
- The Missing Z-Axis: Why this stick does not feature twist rudder, and how to adapt your nosewheel steering and taxi bindings.
- Force Feedback & Telemetry: Feeling subtle telemetry vibrations during gear and flap deployment, and how the stick actively centers under load.

Because getting the best response out of the Moza MA3F requires proper software versions and curve profiles, make sure you are running Moza Cockpit v1.1.5.41 or newer. You can also grab my custom flight-tested MSFS control profiles from the repository linked below.
